column2: On the authority of Abū Burdah, from his father, Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī, that the Prophet ﷺ sent him to Yemen, and he asked him about drinks that were made there. He said: “What are they?”
He said: “Al-bitʿ and al-mizr.” Abū Burdah was asked: “What is al-bitʿ?”
He said: “Honey wine, and al-mizr is barley wine.” He said: “Every intoxicant is unlawful.” Recorded by al-Bukhārī.
Among the drinks in use in Yemen when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī there were al-bitʿ,
which is honey wine, and al-mizr, which is barley wine. Abū Mūsā (may Allah be pleased with him) asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about these two drinks,
and he answered him with a comprehensive answer that covers them and others, saying: “Every intoxicant is unlawful.” The Prophet ﷺ thus tied the prohibition to intoxication,

which shows that any drink that intoxicates is unlawful, and whatever does not intoxicate is lawful. In Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī (5598) it is reported that Abū al-Juwayriyah said: I asked Ibn ʿAbbās about al-bādhiq.

He said: “Muḥammad ﷺ preceded al-bādhiq: whatever intoxicates is unlawful.” He said: “[Then what of] the lawful, wholesome drink?” He said: “After the lawful and wholesome there is nothing but the unlawful and foul.” Ibn Sīdah mentioned in al-Muḥkam that al-bādhiq is one of the names of wine
At first the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had forbidden steeping [drinks] in certain vessels, as is reported in the hadith of the delegation of ʿAbd al-Qays,
reported by al-Bukhārī (53) and Muslim (23). Later he ﷺ abrogated that, as reported in the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Ḥuṣayb (may Allah be pleased with him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “I forbade you to visit graves, but [now] visit them; I forbade you [to keep] the meat of sacrifices beyond three days, but [now] keep whatever you wish;
and I forbade you nabīdh except in a waterskin, but [now] drink from all vessels, and do not drink anything intoxicating.” Reported by Muslim (977).
Everything that intoxicates is unlawful, whether drink or food, liquid or solid, powder, leaf or anything else; for all of it falls under the Prophet's words ﷺ: “Every intoxicant is unlawful.”

Khamr (wine) is whatever clouds the mind and covers it, so everything of that kind falls under the Prophet's words ﷺ, “Every intoxicant is unlawful.” Whatever intoxicates in large amounts, a small amount of it is unlawful, to block the means that lead to intoxication,

whether it is from grapes or something else. Some scholars of al-Kūfah are reported to have held that a small amount that does not intoxicate, if it is not from grapes, may be drunk; but this is not correct,

because it is established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in the hadith of Jābir and others (may Allah be pleased with them), that the Prophet ﷺ said: “Whatever intoxicates in large amounts, a small amount of it is unlawful.” Recorded by Abū Dāwūd (3681),

al-Tirmidhī (1865) and Ibn Mājah (3393). This is general wording covering every intoxicant, whether from grapes or something else. So it is not permissible to consume any intoxicant, except a very small amount to clear a choking.
The Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) were eager to know the rulings of the Sharīʿah.
The Sharīʿah is perfect and contains general, universal principles, as this hadith shows.
Every intoxicant, of whatever kind, is unlawful.
